Lemon Bars with Shortbread Crust⏱ 3 hr 15 min🍽 Makes 16 barsMedium▾

A thick, tart lemon curd layer set over buttery shortbread, cut into squares and dusted with powdered sugar. Sharp enough to make you sit up, rich enough to feel like a real dessert.

Make AheadPotluckCitrus
Prep
20 min
Cook
55 min
Total
3 hr 15 min
Serves
Makes 16 bars
▶️ Watch it made📷 See real photos

1 Ingredients

Tap each one as you gather it.

Batch

Shortbread crust

Lemon filling

Finishing

2 How to make it

Tap a step when it is done.

  1. Line the pan
    Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) with a rack in the center. Line a 9x13-in (23x33 cm) metal baking pan with a parchment sling that overhangs the two long sides by 2 in (5 cm), then lightly butter the short ends. The sling is how you get the whole slab out in one piece for clean cutting; digging bars out of a pan destroys the first row every time.
  2. Cream the shortbread
    Beat the room-temperature butter and granulated sugar with a paddle attachment on medium for 2 minutes until light and fluffy, scraping the bowl once. Add the flour and salt and mix on low just until a soft, crumbly dough forms that holds together when pressed. Stop as soon as it comes together — overworked shortbread bakes up hard rather than tender and sandy.
  3. Press and chill
    Dump the dough into the lined pan and press it into an even layer with your fingers, then smooth it flat with the bottom of a measuring cup, building a slight 1/4-in (6 mm) lip up the sides. An even thickness bakes evenly; thin patches burn while thick ones stay raw. Chill the pressed crust in the freezer for 15 minutes so the butter is cold going into the oven.
  4. Bake the crust fully
    Bake the crust for 20 to 25 minutes, until it is uniformly light golden brown and set to the touch, not pale and soft. A fully baked crust is what keeps the bottom crisp under a wet filling — pulled early, it goes soggy overnight. Leave the oven on and start the filling while the crust bakes.
  5. Zest before juicing
    Zest the lemons with a microplane before you cut them, taking only the yellow and none of the white pith, which is bitter. Then roll each lemon firmly under your palm on the counter before juicing to break the membranes and get significantly more juice out. You need a full 1 cup (240 ml) of juice, so buy an extra lemon or two for insurance.
  6. Whisk the filling
    Whisk the eggs and sugar together in a large bowl for 1 minute until smooth and pale, then whisk in the zest, lemon juice, flour, and salt until completely lump-free. Whisk gently rather than beating air into it, since foam bakes into a pale crust on top of the bars. Let the mixture rest 2 minutes and skim any foam that rises.
  7. Pour onto the hot crust
    Pour the filling directly over the hot crust as soon as it comes out of the oven, right in the pan on the oven rack if you can manage it safely. The hot surface immediately begins setting the bottom of the curd, which is what prevents that thin gummy layer between crust and filling. Pour slowly and evenly across the whole surface.
  8. Bake until just set
    Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the filling is set from edge to center and only the middle 2 in (5 cm) has a very slight jiggle when you nudge the pan. The surface should look matte with a faint pale skin and should not brown. An instant-read thermometer in the center should read about 175°F (79°C); above 185°F (85°C) the eggs curdle and weep.
  9. Cool completely
    Cool the pan on a wire rack to room temperature, about 1 hour. The curd continues to firm as it cools and cutting it warm gives you a shattered mess. Do not cover it while it is warm — trapped steam condenses on the surface and makes it sticky.
  10. Chill before cutting
    Refrigerate the cooled pan, uncovered, for at least 1 hour or up to overnight. A cold slab cuts into crisp-edged squares that hold their shape, while a room-temperature one drags and smears. Then lift out the slab by the sling onto a cutting board.
  11. Cut and dust
    Cut a 4 by 4 grid with a long sharp knife, wiping the blade clean with a hot damp towel between every cut. Dust with powdered sugar through a fine sieve immediately before serving, not before storing — the sugar dissolves into the moist curd within an hour and disappears. Serve cold or at cool room temperature.
Know when it is done
Bake the crust at 350°F (175°C) for 20 to 25 minutes until golden, then bake the filling 30 to 35 minutes until the center reads about 175°F (79°C) and barely jiggles; past 185°F (85°C) the custard curdles.
Serve it with
A pot of Earl Grey, or a glass of Prosecco on a warm afternoon.

3 Chef tips

  • ◆Use only fresh lemon juice. Bottled juice has a dull, slightly metallic taste that is impossible to hide when it is the main flavor of the dish.
  • ◆Bars keep 4 days in an airtight container in the fridge with parchment between the layers. They also freeze up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge and re-dust with sugar.
  • ◆If the filling weeps a little liquid after chilling, it was slightly overbaked. Blot gently with a paper towel before dusting and no one will know.
  • ◆For lime bars, substitute the same volume of fresh lime juice and zest. For a Meyer lemon version, cut the sugar to 2 cups (400 g) since they are much sweeter.
  • ◆Make the crust dough up to 3 days ahead and keep it pressed in the pan, wrapped, in the fridge. It bakes straight from cold with no changes.
